senses.gloss: ch. = h.נָשַׁר , to fall off, drop; to fall apart, decay; to become wearied, faint.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 40:7">Targ. Is. XL, 7</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 64:5">Ib. LXIV, 5</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 21b:14">B. Mets. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>דנַתְרָא</he> that it (the fig) dropped (and was not taken off the tree).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 21b:15">Ib.</cite> <he>אע״ג דנַתְרִין זיתי וכ׳</he> even when the olives have dropped &c.
<cite ref="Shabbat 33b:9">Sabb. 33ᵇ</cite> <he>וקא נַתְרָן דמעת עיניה</he> and the tears fell from his eyes; a. fr.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Ruth 2:16">Targ. Ruth II, 16</cite>.

<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Exodus 9:32">Targ. Y. II, Ex. IX, 32</cite> <he>ואַתְּרַת</he> (not <he>ואִתָּ׳</he>).—Y. Kil. VII, beg. 30ᵈ <he>דמַתְּרָן טרפיהן וכ׳</he> where trees shed their leaves even in midsummer.
<cite ref="Nazir 42a:13">Naz. 42ᵃ</cite> <he>אדמה דלא מַתְּרָא</he> an earth which does not cause falling out of the hair; a. e.—Y. Yeb. XVI, 15ᵈ <he>אתרין</he>, v. infra.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 9b:14">B. Kam. 9ᵇ</cite> <he>בור דרכה לנַתּוּרֵי</he> a pit is liable to fall in (and mere covering it up is not a sufficient precaution).

<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 1:30">Targ. Is. I, 30</cite>; a. e.—Y. Yeb. XVI, 15ᵈ (if one says of a person) <he>נַתְּרִי פלוני</he>, ‘I have dropped that man’, you must not allow his wife to marry again (it does not necessarily mean that he saw him dead), for I may say, he means [read:] <he>אַתְּרִי לפלוני מאכל</he> I dropped that man something to eat.
